name: TeraWulf

logo.source: investors.terawulf.com site header logo (horizontal wolf-shield lockup, image.svg); en.wikipedia infobox has no logo and Commons has none

description: TeraWulf owns and builds power-heavy data-center campuses and is replacing its bitcoin mining with long-term leases of that space to AI companies. Its tenants pay rent per kilowatt of critical power: Core42 (60 MW, 10-year leases), Fluidstack (378 MW at Lake Mariner, New York, 10-year leases, with Google promising to cover Fluidstack's rent if it defaults and receiving 73.6 million penny warrants in return), and Anthropic (401 MW in Kentucky, 20 years, about $19 billion over the term, signed 2026-07-06). In the first half of 2026 HPC leasing was 67% of revenue ($53.0M) and bitcoin mining 33% ($25.8M), against 10% and 90% in all of 2025. Only 81 MW of leased capacity was billing on 2026-06-30. Reported losses are huge ($1.37 billion in H1 2026) because the Google warrants are revalued every quarter as the share price moves, a non-cash charge of $972 million in the half; underneath, the two segments earned $29.4M before overhead.

hq.note: 9 Federal Street, Easton, MD; incorporated in Delaware (FY2025 10-K cover and Item 1)

employees.note: 141 full-time employees including Beowulf E&D, as of the date of the FY2025 10-K (filed 2026-02-27)

businessLines.name: HPC Leasing
businessLines.how: Tenants pay monthly base rent per kilowatt of critical power under long leases (Core42 and Fluidstack 10 years with two five-year renewals; Anthropic 20 years with two five-year renewals), with annual escalation on the Fluidstack leases. Power is passed through without markup, and maintenance and security are billed as separate service components. Core42 prepaid $90.0M, equal to its first 12 months of base rent for 60 MW (derived: about $1.5M per MW per year, before later change orders). Rent starts only when each data hall is delivered.
businessLines.description: Leasing finished data-center space and power at the Lake Mariner campus (Barker, New York) to Core42 and Fluidstack; Anthropic (Kentucky) and Fluidstack (Texas, sold) are the next phases.
businessLines.revenueNote: Rent $44,485K, power pass-through $2,991K, maintenance and other $5,478K. Q2 2026 alone: $31,932K. FY2025: $16,899K (10% of revenue). Revenue came from two customers.

businessLines.name: Digital Asset Mining
businessLines.how: Provides computing power to a bitcoin mining pool and is paid in bitcoin, so revenue follows the bitcoin price and network difficulty. Power is the main cost (gross power cost $25.2M in H1 2026) and is not passed on to anyone.
businessLines.description: Bitcoin mining for its own account at Lake Mariner: about 53,700 miners owned, about 28,300 operating, and 145 MW of legacy mining capacity energized on 2026-06-30 (down from 245 MW on 2025-12-31 as space is repurposed to HPC).

brands.name: Lake Mariner Data Campus (Barker, NY)
brands.segment: HPC Leasing and Digital Asset Mining
brands.share: 438 MW contracted HPC (60 Core42 + 378 Fluidstack); 81 MW billing and 145 MW legacy mining on 2026-06-30

brands.name: Justified Data Campus (Hawesville, KY)
brands.share: 401 MW leased to Anthropic of up to 480 MW gross power

brands.name: Muskie Data Campus (Grayson, KY)
brands.share: 1 GW contracted power from Kentucky Power; bought 2026-05-22 for $30M cash, $50M deferred a year and up to $50M contingent at $100,000 per MW over 1,000 MW

brands.name: Beowulf Electricity & Data LLC (Beowulf E&D)
brands.share: Wholly owned since 2025-05-21; supplies construction, operations and power expertise

brands.name: Abernathy Joint Venture (FS CS 1 LLC)
brands.share: Was 50.1% owned; entire interest sold 2026-07-06 for about $530.0M

whatsNext.text: Fluidstack leases at Lake Mariner commence data hall by data hall in 2H 2026 and early 2027; Google backstop becomes effective as each lease commences
Anthropic lease at Justified (401 MW): initial capacity delivered 2H 2027, full delivery early 2028
Muskie: first 500 MW phase targeted to start ramping in 2028; second 500 MW moved from 2030 to 2029 subject to Kentucky Public Service Commission approval; energy service to start Q4 2028
Abernathy stake sale for about $530.0M cash, received in installments in 2026 and 2027

Revolving credit facility upsized to about $400M with an uncommitted $150M accordion on 2026-10-23; company also seeking more senior secured debt to support letters of credit for utility power commitments
$50.0M deferred cash payment for Muskie due on the first anniversary of the 2026-05-22 closing
